audits.title: Audit of Lithium Monitoring in a Mental Health for Older Persons (Dublin North City Central) Service
audits.standard: Irish Medication Safety Network (IMSN) guidance for prescribing and monitoring lithium therapy
audits.setting: Mental Health Service for Older Persons, Dublin North City Central (community)

cycle1.result: Poor compliance with lithium monitoring against the standard (figures not stated).

audits.intervention: Lithium monitoring pack inserted into patient files to prompt standardised monitoring

cycle2.result: Improvement in recording of blood monitoring (figures not stated).

audits.other_findings: A formal lithium clinic was recommended; the pack will be added to NCHD induction and MDT teaching.
audits.citation: Murphy F. Audit of Lithium Monitoring in a Mental Health for Older Persons (Dublin North City Central) Service. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.118.

audits.title: Audit: lithium monitoring for psychiatric inpatients and community patients during the initiation phase
audits.standard: BNF and trust guidelines: baseline FBC, renal function and electrolytes, thyroid function, BMI (ECG if cardiovascular disease) before lithium, then weekly lithium levels until 4 weeks after stable dose
audits.setting: Inpatients and community patients, Leicestershire Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline FBC 86.71%, renal function 92.19%, thyroid function 89.06%, BMI 77.34%; ECG in 26/36 with cardiovascular disorder; lithium level at one week 84.37%, weekly monitoring 69.53%; weekly monitoring for 4 weeks after stable dose in only 16/128.

audits.other_findings: Lithium levels were not adequately monitored after dose escalations.
audits.citation: Chari D, Abbas M, Dhesi K. Audit: lithium monitoring for psychiatric inpatients and community patients during the initiation phase. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S70-S70. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.227.

audits.title: An audit of lithium prescribing practices in an old age psychiatry service highlighting renal impairment in this cohort
audits.standard: NICE 2014, BNF 2019 and Maudsley 2018: 3-monthly serum lithium and renal tests, thyroid and calcium monitoring
audits.setting: Psychiatry of Old Age service, North-West of Ireland

cycle1.result: 78% (n = 14) on track for 3-monthly lithium levels; 39% (n = 7) in therapeutic range; 83% (n = 15) 3-monthly renal tests; thyroid function 89% (n = 16); calcium documented 63%.

audits.other_findings: All 18 had abnormal renal function; 56% of those started by the service had renal impairment before initiation.
audits.citation: Valentine L, Cannon J, Marmion S, Corcoran M, Cryan M, McCarthy G, et al.. An audit of lithium prescribing practices in an old age psychiatry service highlighting renal impairment in this cohort. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S109-S110. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.323.

audits.title: Audit of shared-care lithium monitoring in a large rural GP practice
audits.standard: Shared care lithium monitoring agreement (individualised by age and comorbidity)
audits.setting: Large rural GP practice under shared-care agreement with local mental health trust

cycle1.result: 26% of those needing annual ECG had one in the past year; 78% had lithium level in previous 3 months; 81% had renal function within requirements; 52% had lipids in previous year

audits.other_findings: Standards linked to a QOF incentive were more often met; lithium QOF indicators were retired in April 2019.
audits.citation: Cranshaw T. Audit of shared-care lithium monitoring in a large rural GP practice. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S316-S317. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.834.

audits.title: Audit of Lithium in a Psychiatry of Old Age Service
audits.standard: NICE guidelines for lithium prescribing and monitoring
audits.setting: Mental Health Service for the Elderly team, County Monaghan (Cavan and Monaghan Mental Health Service)

cycle1.result: All 3-monthly lithium levels completed; 100% given information booklets, record books and BMI recorded; 60% of six-monthly lithium levels completed; 20% of six-monthly bloods done but not documented.

cycle2.result: 100% completed three- and six-monthly lithium levels, with 100% documentation.

audits.other_findings: Recommended a lithium clinic with blood pathways, reminder letters, recording tables, alert cards and written information.
audits.citation: Ateem S. Audit of Lithium in a Psychiatry of Old Age Service. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S149-S149. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.426.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Blood Monitoring of Lithium in Outpatients of Working Age Under Dudley Mental Health Services
audits.standard: NICE CG185; locally agreed 3-monthly lithium levels, 6-monthly U&Es and TFTs, and lithium results reviewed and documented at every outpatient review
audits.setting: Working-age adult outpatients, 8 sector teams, Dudley mental health services

cycle1.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 10%; 4 or more lithium tests in 12 months 17.5%; mean 2.67 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 67.5%.

cycle2.result: 3-monthly lithium monitoring 17.5%; 4 or more tests 32.5%; mean 3.3 tests per patient; results documented at clinic review 62.5%; U&Es 6-monthly 90%; TFTs 6-monthly 85%.

audits.other_findings: A lithium blood monitoring clinic was proposed to improve compliance.
audits.citation: Bridgewater P, Kumar P. Re-Audit of Blood Monitoring of Lithium in Outpatients of Working Age Under Dudley Mental Health Services. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S151-S151. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.406.

audits.title: Quality Improvement Project: Lithium Monitoring in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team
audits.standard: Nine standards from NICE and Trust guidelines (e.g. lithium level 3-monthly, kidney function 3–6-monthly, calcium 6-monthly); target 100%
audits.setting: South Gloucestershire Later Life Community Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: Average compliance 57%; six of eight standards below 60%, including lithium levels, kidney function and calcium.

audits.intervention: Physical health nursing team took over investigations from primary care using a bespoke database, plus a staff education session (PDSA).

cycle2.result: Average compliance 94%; lithium level, kidney function and calcium monitoring 100%.

audits.other_findings: Weight/BMI every 6 months and documented action plans for out-of-range results remained weak; a second PDSA cycle is planned.
audits.citation: Nechowska A, Holman R. Quality Improvement Project: Lithium Monitoring in an Older Adult Community Mental Health Team. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S155-S155. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.402.

audits.standard: National guidance on pre-lithium checks (weight/BMI/waist, TFTs, calcium, eGFR), POMH lithium audit

audits.title: An Audit of Physical Health and Blood Test Monitoring in Patients Under the Care of Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Prescribed Lithium
audits.standard: NICE guidelines: six-monthly TFTs, calcium, eGFR and serum lithium in maintenance; weight/BMI/waist circumference within 12 months; compared with POMH national performance
audits.setting: Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust (POMH lithium audit participation)

cycle1.result: Six-monthly calcium 64%, TFTs 78%, eGFR 83%, serum lithium 87%; weight/BMI/waist within 12 months 71%.

audits.intervention: Planned: Quality Performance Alert to medical and nursing staff and lithium monitoring added to junior doctor induction.
audits.other_findings: TFT and weight/BMI monitoring were above the POMH national level; serum lithium, eGFR and calcium were below it.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Chinnari G, Elhaj-Houssen T, Orrell R. An Audit of Physical Health and Blood Test Monitoring in Patients Under the Care of Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust Who Are Prescribed Lithium. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S237-S237. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.578.

audits.title: Are We Monitoring Our Lithium Patients as Well as We Should be? A Two-Cycle Audit Evaluating Lithium Clinic Documentation in a District General Hospital in Wales
audits.standard: NICE lithium guidance and GMC Good Medical Practice; 100% of relevant data documented
audits.setting: Lithium clinic, Older Person's Mental Health Service, Princess of Wales Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Dose, level and renal function over 83.3% (n = 15); psychotropics 61.1%; side effects 50%; mood 77.8%; safety netting 11.1% (n = 2)

audits.intervention: Results disseminated to team and lithium clinic proforma introduced, revised after clinician feedback

cycle2.result: Dose, levels, psychotropics and side effects 100% (n = 12); renal function and mood 91.7% (n = 11); safety netting 75% (n = 9)

audits.other_findings: Documentation varied between clinicians before the proforma.
audits.citation: Mohammed H, Islam R, Sparrow C, Chan T. Are We Monitoring Our Lithium Patients as Well as We Should be? A Two-Cycle Audit Evaluating Lithium Clinic Documentation in a District General Hospital in Wales. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S249-S250. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.604.

audits.title: Evaluation of Lithium Monitoring Practices for Patients in a Community Mental Health Team: An Audit Report.
audits.standard: NICE NG181 and local standards: serum lithium every 3 months; renal, thyroid and calcium every 6 months; side effect monitoring; fully met 91-100%
audits.setting: Enhanced Teams, Folly Hall Community Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: Lithium levels every 3 months 44.4%; renal function 94.4%; thyroid function 88.9%; calcium 61.1%; side effect monitoring 100%.

audits.other_findings: No action taken for one patient with out-of-range lithium. Recommended reminders, a lithium registry, business meeting discussion and a lithium champion; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Nafiu A, Siddique U, Moyal D. Evaluation of Lithium Monitoring Practices for Patients in a Community Mental Health Team: An Audit Report. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S261-S261. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10642.

audits.title: From Guidelines to Practice: A Lithium Monitoring Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: NICE guidance and local shared-care protocols for lithium monitoring
audits.setting: Five inpatient rehabilitation wards, Royal Edinburgh Hospital

cycle1.result: Urine ACR absent in all patients; serum calcium and thyroid function missed in about 60%; over 10% of results supratherapeutic; renal function not consistently rechecked after high levels.

audits.other_findings: Several patients had overdue lithium, renal or thyroid tests. Planned next steps are standardised lithium order sets and MDT education.
audits.citation: Derouiche E, Sherrie D, Ross S. From Guidelines to Practice: A Lithium Monitoring Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S4-S5. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11157.

audits.title: An Audit and Re Audit of Prelithium Workup in Psychiatry Inpatient Unit of Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad
audits.setting: Psychiatry inpatient unit, Allied Hospital 2, Faisalabad (tertiary care)

cycle1.result: LFTs 50/72 (69.4%); TFTs 3 (4.2%); ECG 14 (19.4%); weight measured in none.

audits.intervention: Results discussed at a departmental meeting with a faculty-led presentation on guidelines and targeted teaching for all residents.
audits.other_findings: Weight measurement remained below 40%. Ongoing education, standardised pre-lithium checklists and regular re-audit were recommended.

audits.title: Lithium in Older Adults: A Community Services Audit and Service Development Project Focusing on Blood Monitoring, Clinic Assesments and GP Correspondence
audits.standard: NICE and Maudsley lithium monitoring guidelines
audits.setting: Psychiatry of old age community services, North Dublin Mental Health Services for Older People

cycle1.result: Deficiencies in documenting side effects and interactions and in regular monitoring of eGFR and physical health (no figures given).

audits.intervention: Lithium flowsheets for 3-monthly bloods, lithium stickers for nursing documentation, a two-page tick-box assessment form, a GP template prompting blood tests and a formal lithium policy.

cycle2.result: Significant improvements in lithium monitoring and documentation reported (no figures given).

audits.other_findings: Patient education and documentation of side effects improved.
audits.citation: Khan H, Hally O. Lithium in Older Adults: A Community Services Audit and Service Development Project Focusing on Blood Monitoring, Clinic Assesments and GP Correspondence. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S312-S312. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11679.

audits.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Compliance With NICE Guidelines for Lithium Monitoring at Kilbarrack East CMHT, Dublin: Audit Cycle Overview
audits.standard: NICE guidelines for lithium monitoring (lithium levels, renal and thyroid function, calcium, BMI)
audits.setting: Kilbarrack East Community Mental Health Team, North Dublin Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: 12% (3/25) compliant with all lithium monitoring guidelines; none had calcium or BMI recorded

audits.intervention: MDT meeting; green sticker system, lithium monitoring sheet, patient monitoring lists defining responsibilities, lithium blood clinic and new Clinical Nurse Specialist reporting system (March 2025)

cycle2.result: 68% (17/25) compliant; 32% (8/25) had no lithium level; 44% had no U&E or thyroid tests; 8% had calcium tested; no BMI recorded

audits.other_findings: Patient education leaflet introduced after the second audit; calcium and BMI stayed poor.
audits.citation: Haroon U, Rauf T, Okogwu L. Comprehensive Evaluation of Compliance With NICE Guidelines for Lithium Monitoring at Kilbarrack East CMHT, Dublin: Audit Cycle Overview. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S299-S299. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11706.

audits.title: Improving Compliance with Lithium Monitoring Guidelines through a Nurse-Led Clinic: A Full Clinical Audit Cycle
audits.standard: NICE: 6-monthly TFTs and U&Es, documented lithium levels, clinical review of results and structured follow-up
audits.setting: General adult community mental health service, HSE North Dublin Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: Fell short across all standards, with deviations of 21% to 36%.

audits.intervention: Nurse-led lithium monitoring clinic (January 2025) with structured appointments, reminders, GP collaboration and systematic documentation, plus team psychoeducation.

cycle2.result: All parameters over 85% compliance; largest gain in documentation and clinical sign-off of investigations (+29.2%).

audits.citation: Ali M, Quigley N, Dolan D. Improving Compliance with Lithium Monitoring Guidelines through a Nurse-Led Clinic: A Full Clinical Audit Cycle. European Psychiatry. 2026;69(S1):S228-S229. doi:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2026.10431.
